props._notes: The client strip, the same block the other act pages carry.

props.html: Firstwater is a sound bath led by one facilitator, and if you’ve been to one you already know how to arrive: lie down, get warm, and rest. The facilitator composes the music for each session, plays live instruments over it, and mixes the whole thing from the floor, lying where your people will lie. The facilitator treats the venue like a studio and tunes the sound system to it, so if you have a space, Firstwater can make it sound like a different one.

Your people come in to low light and lie down, and the mats and blankets are already there. The session opens with ceremony, then there are seventy-five minutes of sound strong enough to feel in your chest and soft enough to rest inside, with real silence partway through, and it closes the same way. Nobody is asked to share, to speak, or to be anywhere but on the floor. Some people follow the guidance closely, some drift, and some sleep, and each of those is a fine way to spend the hour. Afterward there’s tea near the door, and people stay awhile or slip out as they please.

props.title: Four ways a sound bath gets booked.

rows.text: One venue and one session, at your office or in a partner space in Denver, for a wellness week, a quarter close, or the month a team earned something quiet. It’s the simplest of the four.

Firstwater builds one or more sessions into the agenda with you, and uses them to close an evening or open a morning, which is where a sound bath does its best work. A team that has spent the day in meetings gets seventy-five minutes with nothing to do.

When a company is doing a hard thing well, this is a session for the people leaving and for the team that stays, and it’s usually the employer who books it. The page for it on Firstwater’s own site is called Laid Off, and it’s written for the people who’ll be in it.

A private sound bath for the wedding party, the bachelorette, or the couple, at the house you rented, your venue, or a partner space in Denver. It goes into the weekend as the welcome evening, the morning of, or the day after for whoever stayed, and the weddings page covers the music for the rest of it.

props.html: Where a sound bath sits in an offsite week, beside the evenings the music covers, is in company offsite ideas in Colorado for remote teams. During the day, for a yoga studio, a senior center, a hospice, a school or an office at lunchtime, the daytime sound bath page covers where it books and what a venue needs.

props.html: The longer answers, what people wear, whether anyone has to talk, what happens if someone feels a lot or nothing, are on Firstwater’s own FAQ.

items.q: What is a corporate sound bath?
items.a: A group sound bath brought to a company, with a ceremony to open and close it and seventy-five minutes of live sound while your people rest. Some people call it sound healing or sound meditation, and it's the same session. Firstwater is booked through Signet Artists in Denver.

items.q: Can Firstwater bring a sound bath to our office or offsite venue?
items.a: Yes. Firstwater brings the sound system, the mats, the blankets and the waivers to your venue, or the session runs in a partner space in Denver.

items.q: How much space does a sound bath need?
items.a: Enough floor for your people to lie down, a standard outlet, and about ninety minutes ahead of doors. Everything else, from the mats to the waivers, arrives with the facilitator.
Hospitals, hospices, libraries, schools and conference organizers, and couples for a private sound bath on a wedding weekend or a bachelorette, at the house they rented or a partner space in Denver.
